Why it exists

Most LinkedIn advice is too vague to act on.

“Add keywords. Tell your story. Show your passion.” None of that says what a recruiter’s search actually matches, or what they see in the first line on a phone.

LinkedInRank reads the PDF export of a profile and checks it against 30+ signals recruiters filter by: the job title in the headline, the first 120 characters shown on mobile, numbers in experience bullets and the core skills. Then it writes the fixes.

How it works

  1. 1

    Export your profile

    LinkedIn can save any profile as a PDF.

  2. 2

    Drop the file

    It is read in memory. Nothing is stored.

  3. 3

    Get the audit

    A score for each signal, with rewrites for the weak parts.

What it does

Built for Job seekers and professionals who want to show up and stand out in recruiter searches.

  1. 01

    30+ recruiter signals

    Scores headline positioning, keyword discoverability, About structure, quantified experience and completeness.

  2. 02

    Keyword gaps

    Finds the missing keywords and high-intent skills recruiters search for.

  3. 03

    Rewrites

    Suggests stronger headlines and experience bullets, with mobile character-cutoff checks.

  4. 04

    13 free tools

    Headline and About generators, experience rewriter, keyword analyzer, connection notes, post hooks and more.

  5. 05

    Private by design

    Uploads are processed in temporary memory and never stored.

Independent tool. Not affiliated with or endorsed by LinkedIn Corporation.

Inside the product

Real screens from linkedinrank.com, captured 12 November 2026. Select any one to enlarge it.

Decisions that shaped it

A PDF, not a login
The tool never asks for a LinkedIn password and does not scrape anything. The PDF you export is the only input.
Nothing is kept
Uploads are processed in temporary memory and never stored, so there is no account to make.
Fixes over grades
A score on its own is not useful. Every weak signal comes with a suggested rewrite you can paste in.
Independent
LinkedInRank is not affiliated with or endorsed by LinkedIn Corporation, and the site says so.
